h1: Car window tinting in Ticino: law and prices
estratto: What Swiss law says, which windows you can tint, prices and how long the films last: the practical guide from VAM Deco.

paragrafi: Tinting your car windows means more privacy, protection from the sun and greater driving comfort. In Switzerland, however, there are specific rules about which windows you can tint. Here's what to know before you choose, with advice from VAM Deco and thousands of installations behind us.

sezioni.heading: What Swiss law says
paragrafi: The rear side windows and the rear windscreen can be tinted freely, with no limit on the shade, provided the car has both exterior rear-view mirrors. For these windows, the film does not need any type approval.

The front side windows and the windscreen, on the other hand, cannot be tinted: they must keep at least 70% light transmission, as required by art. 71a of the ordinance on the technical requirements for vehicles. During a check or the roadworthiness test, the police can measure the light transmission and penalise values that are too low.

sezioni.heading: Why it's worth it: privacy, sun and comfort
paragrafi: Tinting isn't just about looks. Quality films block up to 99% of UV rays and much of the heat, protecting the interior and reducing how often you need the air conditioning.
lista: Privacy: people outside can't see inside the car.
UV protection: interior and passengers shielded from harmful rays.
Less heat: a cooler cabin and lower air-conditioning use.
Safer driving: less glare, especially at night.

sezioni.heading: How much it costs and how long it lasts
paragrafi: The price depends on the vehicle, the number of windows and the type of film. Tinting the rear side windows and the rear windscreen usually starts from a few hundred francs. We always give you a clear quote before we begin.

When it comes to durability, quality makes the difference: cheap films tend to change colour after 3-4 years, while the professional films we use stay stable over time and are guaranteed for over 10 years.

sezioni.heading: How we work
paragrafi: Every installation follows a method proven on thousands of windows: we assess the vehicle, choose the right shade together, prepare and degrease the surfaces, apply the film with precision and check the result before handover.
The result: no bubbles, no imperfections and work that complies with Swiss regulations. Get in touch for a free consultation and a quote tailored to your car.

faq.domanda: Which car windows can you tint in Switzerland?
faq.risposta: You can freely tint the rear side windows and the rear windscreen, with no limit on the shade, as long as the car has both exterior rear-view mirrors. The front side windows and the windscreen cannot be tinted and must keep at least 70% light transmission.

faq.domanda: Is window tinting legal in Ticino?
faq.risposta: Yes, as long as it follows the Swiss rules: rear side windows and rear windscreen unrestricted, front windows with at least 70% light transmission. Films for the rear windows do not require type approval.

faq.domanda: How much does it cost to tint car windows?
faq.risposta: It depends on the model, the number of windows and the film you choose. For the rear side windows and the rear windscreen, prices start from a few hundred francs. At VAM Deco you get an accurate, free quote before the work begins.

faq.domanda: How long do tinting films last?
faq.risposta: Cheap films can fade after 3-4 years. Professional films, like the ones we use, stay stable over time and are guaranteed for over 10 years.

faq.domanda: Does tinting cause problems at the roadworthiness test?
faq.risposta: No, not if it's compliant. Rear side windows and the rear windscreen cause no problems. On the front windows the police can measure light transmission: keeping the 70% minimum means you pass the check without penalties.
